title: Rumpelstiltskin.
lines: Once upon a time there was a poor miller.
He lived with his daughter in an old mill by the river.
His daughter was kind and pretty and clever.
But the miller had a big mouth.
He liked to say things that weren't true, to impress people.
One day the king came by.
The miller wanted to show off.
My daughter can spin straw into gold!
he said.
That isn't true, of course.
Nobody can spin straw into gold.
But the king loved gold very much.
His eyes began to sparkle.
Bring your daughter to my castle tomorrow, he said.
Then I'll see if it's true.
The next day the girl stood in the castle.
The king took her to a room full of straw.
In the middle stood a spinning wheel.
Spin this straw into gold, said the king.
It must be finished by tomorrow morning.
And he locked the door.
The girl sat on the floor and began to cry.
She had no idea how to spin straw into gold.
Then the door opened.
A strange little man came in.
He had a long beard and a pointy hat.
Why are you crying, girl?
he asked.
I have to spin this straw into gold, she sobbed.
And I don't know how.
What will you give me if I do it?
asked the little man.
My necklace, said the girl.
The little man took the necklace.
He sat down at the spinning wheel.
Whirr, whirr, whirr.
Three turns, and the reel was full of gold.
Whirr, whirr, whirr.
He spun all night long.
And the next morning the room was full of golden thread.
The king was pleased.
But he wanted even more gold.
He took the girl to a bigger room, with even more straw.
Again the girl cried.
Again the little man came.
What will you give me now?
he asked.
My ring, said the girl.
And again the little man spun everything into gold.
On the third night the king took her to the very biggest room.
If you spin this into gold, he said, you will be my queen.
The little man came again.
But the girl had nothing left to give.
Then promise me your first child, when you are queen, said the little man.
The girl was so scared that she said yes.
She thought: Who knows what will happen.
The little man spun everything into gold.
The king married the girl.
She became queen.
A year later she had a sweet little baby.
She was so happy that she had completely forgotten the little man.
But one day he was standing in her room.
Give me what you promised, he said.
The queen got a fright.
She offered him all the gold in the whole kingdom.
But the little man didn't want gold.
She cried so hard that the little man felt a bit sorry for her after all.
I'll give you three days, he said.
If you can guess my name, you may keep your baby.
The queen thought all night.
She sent messengers all over the land to look for names.
On the first day she said: Is your name Caspar?
Melchior?
Balthazar?
No, no, no, laughed the little man.
On the second day she said the silliest names.
Is your name Ribcage?
Muttonbone?
Shoelace?
No, no, no!
On the third day a messenger came back.
I saw something strange, he said.
Deep in the forest, by a little house, there was a small fire burning.
A little man was dancing around it, on one leg.
And he was singing: Today I bake, tomorrow I brew, and then I'll take the queen's child too.
How glad I am that nobody knows that Rumpelstiltskin is my name!
The queen was so happy.
When the little man came, she first said: Is your name Kees?
No!
Is your name Jan?
No!
Is your name perhaps...
Rumpelstiltskin?
The little man went red with rage.
Who told you that?
he shouted.
He stamped his foot so hard that he went through the floor.
And he ran away, into the forest, and he never came back.
The queen held her baby tight.
And the miller?
He never showed off again.
The end.
